about.title: Woodside Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Woodside's rural roads and rolling terrain give the town its character, but the same features—gravel driveways, wooden steps, unlit trails, and older shopping areas along Woodside Road and Portola Road—can create hazards for visitors and residents alike. Falls on private property, at local businesses, or on poorly maintained walkways can lead to fractures, head injuries, or long recovery times that disrupt work and daily life. California premises liability law requires showing the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and failed to address it. That makes early evidence—photos of the hazard, witness names, and incident reports—especially important. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent clients directly; instead, we connect injured people in Woodside with an independent attorney who can evaluate the property owner's responsibility and pursue a claim on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. The consultation and connection are free.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Woodside Premises Case

items.title: Proving the Owner Had Notice
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather the records and testimony needed to establish that notice.

items.title: Racing the Clock on Evidence
items.desc: Surveillance footage at stores and businesses is often erased within days or weeks, so preserving it quickly matters. An independent attorney can send preservation requests before that video disappears.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for a fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. A knowledgeable attorney can help present your case fairly under this rule.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Woodside?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned, such as a county road shoulder or public building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. It's best to have an attorney review the specifics of your fall as soon as possible.

items.question: What if the fall happened on a private ranch or rural property in Woodside?
items.answer: Many properties in Woodside are large private lots, ranches, or wooded parcels, which can raise different questions about maintenance responsibility and visitor status. An attorney can help determine whether the owner had a duty to inspect or warn about the specific hazard, whether it was a loose step, hidden hole, or unmarked drop-off.

items.question: Do I still have a claim if I was partly at fault for the fall?
items.answer: Yes. California's pure comparative fault rule allows you to recover compensation even if you share some responsibility, though your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of fault. An independent attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your specific situation.
